h1: The 6 Best 4K Webcams of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six true 4K webcams compared on sensor, frame rate, low-light handling, mounting and software support for streamers.
summary: The Logitech MX Brio is the best all-round 4K webcam, with true 4K capture, auto light correction and a USB-C connection. The Razer Kiyo Pro Ultra is the creator pick for low light, the Elgato Facecam Pro adds 4K60, and the EMEET C960 is the budget way to try 4K.
intro: Most video calls compress 4K down to 720p or 1080p anyway, so a 4K webcam only pays off when you record or stream locally. Buying one for Zoom alone is the classic mistake, and a good 1080p camera would do just as well there.
We reviewed eight webcams and ranked the six that deliver true 4K, judging sensor, frame rate, light handling, mounting and software support from the spec sheets. We did not capture sample footage.

products.name: Logitech MX Brio Ultra HD 4K Webcam (Graphite)
products.verdict: True 4K, auto light correction and a USB-C cable.
products.description:
The MX Brio captures true 4K UHD, corrects lighting automatically, has a built-in privacy shutter and connects through USB-C. Its wide diagonal field of view suits shared desks. Street cost falls between $100 and $200.

It ranks first because it joins 4K with a modern connector and a shutter, where the older Brio needs USB 3.0 for full resolution. It does not offer the manual controls of the Razer.

It suits people who record content as well as take calls.

products.name: Razer Kiyo Pro Ultra 4K Webcam
products.verdict: A large sensor and DSLR-style manual controls.
products.description:
The Kiyo Pro Ultra pairs 4K with a large sensor, auto light correction, a built-in mic and shutter, and DSLR-style manual controls. It works with OBS, Xsplit, Zoom and Teams and sits in the $200 to $500 band.

It ranks second because it offers the best low-light sensor in the roundup, but it costs a band more than the MX Brio.

It suits streamers who work in dim rooms and want to tune exposure.

products.name: Elgato Facecam Pro, True 4K60 Webcam (Renewed)
products.verdict: The only true 4K at 60 frames per second here.
products.description:
The Facecam Pro records true 4K at 60 frames per second, with advanced light correction, DSLR-style manual controls and a wide-angle lens. This listing is a renewed, refurbished unit in the $200 to $500 band.

It ranks third because smoother 60fps is a real gain for streaming, but refurbished condition carries warranty risk compared with new stock.

It suits streamers who value motion smoothness.

products.name: Logitech Brio Ultra 4K HD Webcam (Black)
products.verdict: True 4K that works with OBS, but needs USB 3.0.
products.description:
The Brio records true 4K with a wide field of view, auto-adjusting light correction and support for OBS and major streaming software. It needs USB 3.0 for full 4K. Street cost falls between $100 and $200.

It ranks fourth since the MX Brio adds USB-C and a privacy shutter at the same band.

It suits streamers who already have a USB 3.0 port.

products.name: Logitech 4K PRO Magnetic Webcam for Apple Pro Display XDR
products.verdict: A magnetic 4K mount made for Apple Pro Display XDR.
products.description:
This 4K webcam uses a magnetic mount designed for the Apple Pro Display XDR, giving stable mounting with no clip-on wobble, in a compact form with a USB connection. The cost is in the $50 to $100 range.

Fifth place reflects that the mount only suits one display, which narrows its audience.

Buy it only if you own the Pro Display XDR.

products.name: EMEET C960 4K Webcam
products.verdict: The cheapest way to try 4K, with autofocus and dual mics.
products.description:
The C960 has a 4K UHD CMOS sensor, PDAF autofocus, dual omnidirectional microphones, a 73 degree field of view and a built-in privacy cover. It sits in the $25 to $50 band.

It ranks last because its sensor is smaller than the premium picks, but it costs a fraction of them.

It suits buyers curious about 4K.

whatMatters.detail: Video call apps often compress to 1080p or less. 4K matters for recording and streaming locally. If you only join meetings, 1080p does the same job. Decide before you pay for resolution.
Frame rate is how many pictures per second the webcam captures. 30fps is fine for calls, while 60fps looks smoother in motion. Check whether 4K is offered at 30 or 60fps.
A larger sensor gathers more light, helping in dim rooms. Auto light correction adjusts exposure. Look for sensor details in the listing.
Full 4K needs enough bandwidth. USB 3.0 or USB-C is required on some models. Confirm you have the port.
DSLR-style controls let you fix exposure and focus. They help creators but add tuning. Look for the manual controls note.

faq.a: Often not, since apps compress. 4K helps recording and streaming.
The Logitech Brio needs USB 3.0 for full 4K, and the MX Brio uses USB-C.
It can save money but check warranty. The Elgato Facecam Pro here is renewed.

faq.q: How do I set it up?
faq.a: Plug it in, install the maker's app if needed and select it in your streaming software.
Use a built-in shutter such as on the MX Brio or the EMEET privacy cover.

faq.q: Does it work on a monitor mount?
faq.a: Most clip on. The Logitech 4K PRO uses a magnetic mount for the Pro Display XDR.

finalTake: The Logitech MX Brio is the best 4K webcam for most buyers, joining true 4K with USB-C and a shutter. Pick the Razer Kiyo Pro Ultra for dim rooms, the Elgato Facecam Pro for 60fps, and the EMEET C960 to try 4K cheaply.
